title: Dallas Fed Texas Manufacturing Outlook Survey (Nov 2026 data)
source: EST: dallasfed.org's Texas Manufacturing Outlook Survey page, re-fetched direct 2026-09-05 (HTTP 200, desktop user-agent) and now quoted VERBATIM from its own markup rather than through a summarizing fetcher — the table headed '2026 release dates' carries the column header `Release (9:30 a.m. CT)` and the row `November | Monday, November 30`, alongside the note that 'The publishing process begins at 9:30 a.m. CT. While we strive to ensure the information is published to our website in a timely manner, we cannot guarantee the exact timing all survey content becomes available online.' Its sibling rows give the rest of 2026 as Jan 26, Feb 23, Mar 30, Apr 27, May 26, Jun 29, Jul 27, Aug 31, Sep 28, Oct 26, Dec 28, and the August report (/research/surveys/tmos/2026/2608, same fetch) independently prints 'Next release: Monday, September 28'. Independently consistent with the series' observed last-Monday-of-month cadence (2026-11-30 is November's last Monday). Stays estimate on the two grounds that survive: the publisher's availability is demonstrably intermittent (HTTP 403 to the 2026-09-01 session, 200 on 09-05), and — the binding one — the source-prefix table in market-events-data.ts has no confirmed tier for a reserve-bank survey page at all (`FED:` is scoped to federalreserve.gov's FOMC calendar), so no source quality can promote this entry from inside any lane. This lane also never self-promotes an adjacency it discovered in-sweep. Note the 10:30 ET time is a process START, not a guaranteed release instant — the publisher declines to guarantee it
notes: The regional analog that lands 45 minutes after the Chicago print on the same morning, and the reason to read the two together: on 2026-08-28 Chicago collapsed to 47.1 (-10.5pt) and three days later this survey printed the mirror image — general business activity 11.6 from 1.3 (a Jan-2025 high), production 16.1 from 10.1, new orders 22.0 from 6.4. Tracking only the analog that missed low leaves the calendar structurally primed to see soft manufacturing signals and not firm ones, which is the selection bias the dallas-fed-mfg-2026-09-28 entry was created to remove. Kept `low`, not `medium` like Chicago, for that entry's reason unchanged: a single-state survey leading the national ISM by a full month is context, not a leading indicator of the next print. The 2026-11-30 instance carries one extra property — the chicago-pmi-2026-11-30 research established that no BEA, Census or BLS release is scheduled that morning (Thanksgiving pulls the month-end 08:30 block to 11-25/11-27), so Chicago 09:45 and this survey 10:30 are the session's only two scheduled macro releases, and the 09:45-09:50 measurement window that ledger's forward tests use closes 40 minutes before this one lands. Discovered during the chicago-pmi-2026-11-30 initial-research adjacency sweep (2026-09-05).
